newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products steady, except softer gasoline.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products steady, except softer gasoline.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products ended mostly steady on Wednesday except for gasoline.

High sulphur fuel oil generated interest with good demand from Romania and limited local supply holding prices stable against weakening crude markets. The dearth in supply saw product moving in from the Caribbean.
Alpine was reported to have booked 75,000 tonnes from the Caribbean to Constanza.
Low sulphur fuel oil was balanced to weak with tight supplies countered by slack demand, but sentiment was generally softer with crude. Cargoes were valued around $106 cif Med.
Gasoline was softer in line with crude and as more refineries came back from maintenance while potential buyers remained elusive on the spot market.
Naphtha was seen as fairly balanced with Asian demand soaking most supply, but small pockets of available material were seen out of Turkey, Libya, Tunisia and Greece.
"Libya is offering some material but I would expect it to reduce in quantity now that the Ras Lanuf cracker is back up and running," said one trader.
Traders were also trying to get a more exact picture of how much material has left the region over the last month.
"If it's a question of some 500,000 tonnes that's not so bad, but if it's 700,000 it really could get quite tight," said another trader.
Gas oil was steady with the market looking balanced, the market taking a lead on Italian 0.2 pct on yesterday's deal of high fob quotes +$4.
"It's between high fob quotes $3-4, but nothing has been done," said one dealer. Russian material was also looking firm with high fob quotes +$4 and high cif +$2 basis Genoa.
